title: You Won’t Get Free of It by Rachel Aviv review – a subtle study of the mother-daughter bond

paragraphs.en: Rachel Aviv has a profound interest in the vagaries of human psychology: Strangers to Ourselves, her last book, profiled five people whose psychiatric states resisted straightforward explanation, testing the limits of the mental health system. A Pulitzer finalist, Aviv has become known for rigorous, penetrating journalism that is as empathic as it is insightful. Now comes You Won’t Get Free of It, six stories of mothers and daughters, all originally published in the New Yorker.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔·阿维夫对人类心理的变幻莫测怀有深刻的兴趣：她的上一本书《陌生的自我》刻画了五位精神状态难以得到简单解释的人，检验了精神健康体系的边界。作为普利策奖决选入围者，阿维夫以严谨、深刻的新闻报道而闻名，她的作品既充满共情又富有洞见。如今她带来了《You Won’t Get Free of It》，收录了六篇关于母女的故事，最初都发表于《纽约客》。

paragraphs.en: Madness runs through this book, too, in the stories of Linda Bishop, a woman who, upon discharge from hospital after a psychotic break, holed up in an abandoned farmhouse and tried to subsist on apples alone, and of Mary, a woman whose delusions and paranoia were only seemingly cured as a side-effect of chemotherapy. It’s also there in the childhood memories of the psychologist Elizabeth Loftus – a professional court witness for those who have been accused of abuse, one of whom was Harvey Weinstein. Loftus’s mother was found drowned, perhaps as a result of suicide. In Aviv’s masterly profile, she teases out a conclusion that leaves you pondering the extent to which this memory expert can rely on her own recollections, and what that says about her particular line of work.
paragraphs.zh: 疯狂也贯穿了这本书：琳达·毕晓普的故事里，这位女性在精神病发作后出院，躲进一座废弃农舍，试图仅靠苹果维持生存；还有玛丽的故事，她的妄想和偏执似乎只是因化疗的副作用才得以“治愈”。疯狂同样存在于心理学家伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯的童年记忆中——她是一位为被指控虐待者出庭作证的专业证人，其中一位当事人就是哈维·韦恩斯坦。洛夫特斯的母亲被发现溺亡，可能是自杀。在阿维夫娴熟的刻画中，她抽丝剥茧地得出一个结论，让你不禁思索：这位记忆专家在多大程度上能信赖自己的回忆，而这又说明了她的这一特殊工作意味着什么。

paragraphs.en: Of the mother representing madness, Marguerite Duras said: “Our mothers always remain the strangest, craziest people we’ve ever met.” Yet there is psychological instability here on the part of daughters, too: Hannah Upp, whose story opens the collection, suffered from fugue states that would lead to her eventual disappearance. Aviv compassionately chronicles her mother’s desperate quest to find her.
paragraphs.zh: 关于作为疯狂化身的母亲，玛格丽特·杜拉斯曾说：“我们的母亲永远是我们遇到过的最奇怪、最疯狂的人。”但在这本书中，女儿们也同样存在心理上的不稳定：以汉娜·厄普的故事开篇的这本文集里，厄普患有神游状态，这最终导致了她的失踪。阿维夫怀着同情记述了她的母亲寻找她的绝望历程。

paragraphs.en: Aviv’s investigation into Munro’s failure to protect her daughter Andrea from abuse is the standout piece here
paragraphs.zh: 阿维夫对门罗未能保护女儿安德烈亚免遭虐待的调查，是本书中最突出的篇章。

paragraphs.en: In the preface, Aviv writes about her interest in the “hide and seek” dynamic of mother-daughter pairings, and indeed, each of these stories could be said to represent an acting out of that game. What is interesting is that Aviv, too, is a player. “It was as if I had failed to see the drama on the mother’s side, too – her particular longings and humiliations and needs,” she writes, of her own journalism.
paragraphs.zh: 在前言中，阿维夫写到自己对母女关系中“捉迷藏”式互动模式的兴趣，事实上，可以说这些故事中的每一个都是这种游戏的具象化演出。有趣的是，阿维夫本人也是玩家。“仿佛我也未能看到母亲那一方的戏剧性——她特有的渴望、屈辱和需求，”她这样谈到自己的新闻报道。

paragraphs.en: Aviv admits to a previous “deficit of curiosity” about mothers. It is admirable how clear-eyed she is about these failures of imagination, which became apparent only after she herself became a mother. In Bishop’s case Aviv neglected to mention, or consider, the possible impact of a baby given up for adoption when Bishop was a young woman. “I had not even asked a follow-up question,” Aviv admits, and you can feel her embarrassment. She has gone back and remedied the “imbalance” for the purposes of this collection, but the discussion itself prompts a fascinating question: to what extent does a woman’s motherhood – or lack thereof – contribute to her perspective as a writer?
paragraphs.zh: 阿维夫坦言自己此前对母亲们存在一种“好奇心缺失”。她对这些想象力的失败看得如此清醒，令人钦佩，而这些失败直到她自己成为母亲后才显现出来。在毕晓普的案例中，阿维夫忽略了提及或考虑毕晓普年轻时送养一个婴儿可能带来的影响。“我甚至没有追问过一个问题，”阿维夫坦言，你能感受到她的尴尬。为了这本文集，她回头修正了这一“失衡”，但这一讨论本身就引出了一个引人入胜的问题：一位女性的母亲身份——或缺乏母亲身份——在多大程度上影响了她作为作家的视角？

paragraphs.en: It is not a question with an easy answer, not least in the case of novelist Alice Munro. Aviv’s investigation into Munro’s utter failure to protect her daughter, Andrea, from the abuse of her partner, Gerry, is the standout piece here. While it is claimed Munro knew of the abuse , was able to make reference to it in her art (Aviv’s tracing of it through Munro’s writing is meticulous), she chose not to act. That choice – the cowardice of it – and its lifelong repercussions for her daughters may never have come fully to light were it not for the persistence of several journalists, Aviv included. Munro emerges a pathetic figure; I have been unable to read her since.
paragraphs.zh: 这不是一个容易回答的问题，尤其是在小说家艾丽丝·门罗的案例中。阿维夫对门罗完全未能保护女儿安德烈亚免受其伴侣格里虐待的调查，是本书中最突出的篇章。虽然据称门罗知道这起虐待，并能将其写进自己的作品（阿维夫在门罗的写作中对其进行的追溯极为细致），她却选择不作为。若非包括阿维夫在内的几位记者的坚持，那一选择——它的怯懦——及其对女儿们终生的影响可能永远不会被完全揭露。门罗由此显露出一个可悲的形象；自那以后，我一直无法再读她的书。

paragraphs.en: However our mothers behave, the fact is we will never truly know them. Aviv writes, not entirely comfortably, of how she is essentially living out her own mother’s dream career. The editorial comments she leaves on Aviv’s work – such as a note about caring for a suicidal friend on an article about mental illness – constitute for her daughter a “chronic delusion of reference”. It’s a neat theory – but as a writer whose mother sometimes gives similarly self-reflective feedback, I found myself wondering if what we have here is simply a mother’s insistence that she was, and remains, a person, if her daughter would only care to look.
paragraphs.zh: 无论我们的母亲如何表现，事实是我们永远无法真正了解她们。阿维夫以并不完全自在的口吻写到，她基本上是在过着自己母亲的梦想职业。母亲在阿维夫作品上留下的编辑意见——比如在一篇关于精神疾病的文章上写下关于照顾一位有自杀倾向的朋友的批注——在女儿看来构成了“一种慢性的自我指涉妄想”。这是个巧妙的理论——但作为一名母亲有时也会给出类似自我投射式反馈的作家，我不禁在想，我们在这里看到的，是否仅仅是一位母亲的坚持：她曾是一个、并且依然是一个有血有肉的人，只要她的女儿愿意去看看。
